actual-force-and-virtual-displacement-or.intuitive_summary: Imagine a ball resting at the bottom of a bowl. It's in equilibrium. If you imagine nudging the ball an infinitesimal amount in any direction *along the surface of the bowl* (a 'virtual displacement'), the net force of gravity does no work. This is because at the very bottom, the force of gravity points straight down, and the infinitesimal nudge is perfectly horizontal. The force and the displacement are perpendicular. If the ball were on the side of the bowl, gravity would have a component along the nudge, doing work and causing the ball to accelerate, proving it wasn't in equilibrium.

mssm-superpotential-formula-113e4eaf.title: Superpotential of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM)
mssm-superpotential-formula-113e4eaf.description: Defines the holomorphic superpotential $W_{\text{MSSM}}$ in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, which encodes the supersymmetric Yukawa interactions and the Higgsino mass term.
mssm-superpotential-formula-113e4eaf.conceptual_definition: The superpotential $W_{\text{MSSM}}$ is a holomorphic function of the chiral superfields of the theory, constructed to be the most general renormalizable function consistent with the gauge symmetries of the Standard Model ($SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$) and R-parity. Its terms dictate the F-term contributions to the scalar potential, fermion masses, and trilinear scalar interactions. The full expression is $W_{\text{MSSM}} = \bar{u} \mathbf{y}_u Q H_u - \bar{d} \mathbf{y}_d Q H_d - \bar{e} \mathbf{y}_e L H_d + \mu H_u H_d$.
mssm-superpotential-formula-113e4eaf.interpretation: The superpotential $W_{\text{MSSM}}$ is a sum of terms, each representing a fundamental interaction. The term $\bar{u} \mathbf{y}_u Q H_u$ describes the Yukawa coupling between the up-type quark superfields ($\bar{u}$, $Q$) and the up-type Higgs superfield ($H_u$), generating masses for up-type quarks. The term $\bar{d} \mathbf{y}_d Q H_d$ similarly describes the Yukawa coupling for down-type quarks with the down-type Higgs superfield ($H_d$). The term $\bar{e} \mathbf{y}_e L H_d$ represents the Yukawa coupling for leptons, involving the lepton superfields ($\bar{e}$, $L$) and the down-type Higgs superfield ($H_d$). The final term, $\mu H_u H_d$, is the supersymmetric Higgs mass term, also known as the $\mu$-term. The parameter $\mu$ has units of mass and its value is critical for phenomenology, contributing to the masses of the Higgsinos (the fermionic superpartners of the Higgs bosons).
mssm-superpotential-formula-113e4eaf.limits_and_boundary: In the limit where the supersymmetry breaking scale $M_{\text{SUSY}} \to \infty$, the contributions of superpartners decouple, and the theory should reduce to the Standard Model. The $\mu$-term, however, presents a challenge known as the $\mu$-problem, as there is no a priori reason for the mass parameter $\mu$ to be near the electroweak scale. If the Yukawa couplings $\mathbf{y}_u, \mathbf{y}_d, \mathbf{y}_e \to 0$, the fermions would be massless. The stability of the electroweak vacuum places constraints on the parameters of the superpotential and the soft supersymmetry-breaking terms.
mssm-superpotential-formula-113e4eaf.symmetry_origin: The structure of the MSSM superpotential is constrained by the gauge symmetries of the Standard Model, $SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$, and by holomorphy, a requirement of $N=1$ supersymmetry. R-parity is an additional discrete symmetry imposed to forbid terms that would lead to rapid proton decay, ensuring lepton and baryon number conservation.

ckm-matrix-unitarity-condition-first-row.title: Unitarity Constraint on the First Row of the CKM Matrix
ckm-matrix-unitarity-condition-first-row.conceptual_definition: In the Standard Model, the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa (CKM) matrix, denoted $V_{CKM}$, is a unitary matrix that connects the mass eigenstates of quarks to their weak interaction eigenstates. The unitarity condition, $V_{CKM} V_{CKM}^\dagger = \mathbb{I}$, ensures the conservation of probability in weak interactions. This specific formula, $|V_{ud}|^2 + |V_{us}|^2 + |V_{ub}|^2 = 1$, represents the first diagonal element (for the up quark) of this matrix identity. It mandates that the total probability of an up quark coupling to any of the down-type quarks ($d, s, b$) is exactly 1.
ckm-matrix-unitarity-condition-first-row.intuitive_summary: Imagine an 'up' quark must change its identity via the weak force. It has three possible 'destinations': a 'down' quark, a 'strange' quark, or a 'bottom' quark. This law is the particle physics version of a simple rule: the chances of all possible outcomes must add up to 100%. The up quark must transition to one of these three options, with no probability 'leaking' out.
ckm-matrix-unitarity-condition-first-row.interpretation: The equation $\sum_{j=d,s,b} |V_{uj}|^2 = 1$ is a specific instance of the CKM matrix unitarity. Each term $|V_{ij}|^2$ represents the probability for a weak transition between an up-type quark $i$ and a down-type quark $j$. Here, $|V_{ud}|^2$ is the probability of an up-to-down quark transition, $|V_{us}|^2$ is the probability of an up-to-strange transition, and $|V_{ub}|^2$ is the probability of an up-to-bottom transition. The sum equaling 1 signifies that these are the only possible outcomes for an up quark's charged-current weak interaction, thus conserving total probability.
ckm-matrix-unitarity-condition-first-row.symmetry_origin: This constraint originates from the unitarity of the transformation matrix between the quark mass and weak eigenbases. This unitarity is a fundamental requirement for a consistent quantum field theory, ensuring the conservation of probability (and thus the norm of state vectors) under time evolution. It is intrinsically linked to the $SU(2)_L$ gauge symmetry of the electroweak interaction in the Standard Model.
ckm-matrix-unitarity-condition-first-row.limits_and_boundary: This equation is an exact identity within the Standard Model framework, not an approximation. A significant deviation from 1 in the experimental measurement of the sum $|V_{ud}|^2 + |V_{us}|^2 + |V_{ub}|^2$ would be a profound discovery. Such a violation of 'first-row unitarity' would strongly indicate the existence of physics beyond the Standard Model, such as a fourth generation of quarks, new gauge bosons, or other exotic particles to which the up quark could couple.
